cost: R requests, P partial results, B bytes: parse/set work O(B+R log R+P log P), partial request lookup O(P*R); storage O(B+R+P). Each remaining request invokes one external process through teacher and one sync_data. Wall time/network/model cost unspecified. No resource cap or crash durability theorem.
description: Restartable local queue with sticky error, worker lock, immutable request snapshot, append-only partial successes and final rename. Live transport is delegated to mova_teacher; bounded tests replace its executable.
forward: run preserves final/error/request/legacy precedence and lock admission; async spawns the current executable, transfers child lock ownership and waits at most five seconds for the exact child PID or successful exited-child final results. finish atomically publishes a synced complete PID. Existing-lock malformed/stale PID failures remain fail-closed. execute preserves validated partial rows and separates an unterminated real record before appending missing successes, then syncs and renames final results.
inverse: A final results file is compatible with fresh execution or a valid prior prefix plus resumed suffix; directory bytes cannot identify which without external logs. Given immutable requests, success rows constrain provider=codex, unique known ids and matching model but do not uniquely reconstruct prompts or actual process behavior.
limitations: Fake executable only; no live Codex/API behavior evidence.
Crash durability, PID reuse, hostile directory mutation, duplicate malformed partial cases not exhaustively executed.
Separator repair covers a real last record lacking LF; whitespace-only tails are left in place; mid-row corruption is refused, not repaired; bare CR after a row is accepted as JSON whitespace.

Startup admission is bounded to a known new Child; timeout retains uncertain work. Existing live PID checks do not authenticate identity; hostile mutation, PID reuse and power-loss remain outside scope.
state: For an unmodified single-worker directory and successful file operations, final publication follows completion of every request; resumed valid successes are not called again. Lock and completion files are trusted filesystem state, not authenticated certificates. Error handling records sticky failure; RAII attempts lock removal and ignores cleanup failure.
